claim.claim-text: a display configured to display a two-dimensional array of input regions, wherein each input region of a subset of the input regions corresponds to a respective hiragana character of a first set of hiragana characters, each hiragana character of the first set represents a combination of a respective consonant with a common vowel, and the display comprises a touch panel configured to detect a touch to any of the input regions; at least one processor and a computer-readable memory storing program instructions that cause the at least one processor to:

in response to detecting a touch to an input region, of the subset of the input regions, that corresponds to a hiragana character of the first set of hiragana characters representing a combination of a given consonant with the common vowel, display an arrangement of hiragana characters in which a plurality of associated hiragana characters are displayed with the hiragana character to which the touched input region corresponds, each associated hiragana character being displayed at a different respective display position relative to a display position of the hiragana character to which the touched input region corresponds, and each associated hiragana character representing a combination of the given consonant with a different respective vowel; and in response to detecting that the detected touch has moved in a direction corresponding to the display position of one of the associated hiragana characters relative to the display position of the hiragana character to which the touched input region corresponds, and has subsequently been released, determine that the corresponding one of the associated hiragana characters has been inputted.

2. The mobile terminal device according to claim 1, wherein the display position of each associated hiragana character relative to the hiragana character to which the touched input region corresponds is fixed according to the different vowel that the associated hiragana character respectively represents, regardless of which input region of the subset of the input regions was touched.

3. The mobile terminal device according to claim 1 or 2, wherein the two-dimensional array of input regions includes a set of ten input regions each of which corresponds to a respective hiragana character, wherein nine input regions of the ten input regions are arranged in three columns and three rows, and a tenth input region of the ten input regions is arranged in a central column of the three columns below a bottom row of the three rows.

4. The mobile terminal device according to claim 3, wherein the tenth input region corresponds to a hiragana character that represents a combination of a further consonant with the common vowel, and for which there is only one associated hiragana character that represents the further consonant with a different vowel.

5. The mobile terminal device according to any preceding claim, wherein, the display position of each associated hiragana character relative to the display position of the hiragana character to which the touched input region corresponds respectively comprises a different one of: a display position above the display position of the hiragana character to which the touched input region corresponds; a display position to the right of the display position of the hiragana character to which the touched input region corresponds; a display position to the left of the display position of the hiragana character to which the touched input region corresponds; or a display position below the display position of the hiragana character to which the touched input region corresponds.

6. The mobile terminal device according to any preceding claim, wherein the program instructions are configured to cause the at least one processor to, in response to detecting that the detected touch has moved in the direction corresponding to the display position of one of the associated hiragana characters relative to the display position of the hiragana character to which the touched input region corresponds, display the corresponding one of the associated hiragana characters in an emphasized style.

8. The method according to claim 7, wherein the display position of each associated hiragana character relative to the hiragana character to which the touched input region corresponds is fixed according to the different vowel that the associated hiragana character respectively represents, regardless of which input region of the subset of the input regions was touched.

9. A method according to claim 7 or 8, wherein the two-dimensional array of input regions includes a set of ten input regions each of which corresponds to a respective hiragana character, wherein nine input regions of the ten input regions are arranged in three columns and three rows, and a tenth input region of the ten input regions is arranged in a central column of the three columns below a bottom row of the three rows.

10. The method according to claim 9, wherein the tenth input region corresponds to a hiragana character that represents a combination of a further consonant with the common vowel, and for which there is only one associated hiragana character that represents the further consonant with a different vowel.

11. The method according to any of claims 7 to 10, wherein, the display position of each associated hiragana character relative to the display position of the hiragana character to which the touched input region corresponds respectively comprises a different one of: a display position above the display position of the hiragana character to which the touched input region corresponds; a display position to the right of the display position of the hiragana character to which the touched input region corresponds; a display position to the left of the display position of the hiragana character to which the touched input region corresponds; or a display position below the display position of the hiragana character to which the touched input region corresponds.

12. The method to any of claims 7 to 11, wherein, in response to detecting that the detected touch has moved in the direction corresponding to the display position of one of the associated hiragana characters relative to the display position of the hiragana character to which the touched input region corresponds, the corresponding one of the associated hiragana characters is displayed in an emphasized style.
